sm: A judge in Birmingham, England has refused to dismiss criminal charges against Isabel Vaughan-Spruce, co-director of March for Life UK, so she will stand trial between January twenty-fifth and twenty-ninth, 2027. She has pleaded not guilty to five charges under the national abortion clinic buffer-zone law, which took effect in October 2024. The charges say she stood silently and prayed outside a clinic, intending to influence people's decisions or being reckless about causing harassment, alarm or distress. She is the first person charged under that law. Her lawyers argued the case was an abuse of process and that silent prayer falls outside what Parliament intended. Vaughan-Spruce said peaceful prayer is not and never can be a crime. She was arrested in 2022 and acquitted in 2023, and she received a thirteen thousand pound settlement from police in August 2024. If convicted, she could face an unlimited fine.
